title: Do NOT mask positive azimuthal outliers on this campaign — they are the LaB6 Bragg rings
rule: If you apply azimuthal sigma-clipping (skills/masking/02), mask NEGATIVE outliers only (shadows / defective pixels). Positive outliers on this campaign are the sample's own Bragg signal: report them, do not mask them. Masking positives is correct ONLY when the product is a strictly isotropic background (not the case for a LaB6 calibration run).
evidence: Measured on agent_trial_07 by re-running skill 02's documented clip (thres 3.0, max_iter 5, 122 radial bins) and splitting the result by sign: 3422 positive vs 127 negative outliers. Masking ALL outliers collapsed the two true lattice rings — ring 847 px contrast 1.3988 -> 0.3191 (C2 minimum 1.0) and ring 1245 px 3.3332 -> 1.0335 (minimum 2.0) — i.e. the run would FAIL its own verifier; mean ring contrast -35.9%, worst ring -77.2%. The only gain was background rel_noise 0.01350 -> 0.01274 (-5.6%), a metric that already had 2.2x margin against its 0.03 limit. Masking negatives only cost 127 px and left every ring contrast unchanged (-0.07% mean).
why: qa/09 indexing shows 847 px = LaB6 (100) and 1245 px = (110) are the only true lattice reflections in range; 367/531/734 px are diffuse anchors. Sigma-clipping damages exactly the two sharp Bragg rings and leaves the diffuse features untouched — the damage is not incidental, it is the method removing the measurement.
scope: Run0475 / xppl1016922, LaB6 powder calibration, Jungfrau1M. Re-evaluate for amorphous or pump-probe samples where an isotropic background IS the product.
conflict_resolved: skills/masking/02 (When to use: 'catches sporadic Bragg') vs skills/masking/11 (Decision rules: 'do not mask positive detections'). Same algorithm, opposite defaults. 11's policy wins on this campaign, by the measurement above.

title: The nominal sample-detector distance (190 mm) is wrong by +3.5% — px positions are sound, q labels are not
rule: Judge ring positions in PIXELS, not in the q values printed by step4_iq.py. When reporting q, state that the axis is derived from the nominal 190 mm and is ~3.4% high, or use D_eff = 196.6 mm.
evidence: Distance-free tan-ratio indexing on agent_trial_06 and _07 (qa/09): observed r(1243)/r(846) = 1.4693 vs predicted (110)/(100) = 1.4712, agreement -0.13%; per-ring effective distance 196.76 and 196.50 mm, spread 0.13%. Against step4_iq.py's nominal 190 mm that is +3.5%, so ring 847 px is labelled q = 1.563 A^-1 when its true value is 1.5115.
why: The tan-ratio test uses only lambda and the lattice constant, so it is independent of the distance being audited. Two rings agreeing to 0.13% on D_eff is a geometry measurement, not a fit.
scope: Current XPP geometry for Run0475. Any detector move invalidates it — re-derive D_eff before reusing.
